title: Sonar-TS: Search-Then-Verify Natural Language Querying for Time Series Databases
claim: Prior approaches fail on morphology or long context; ours searches an index for candidates, then verifies them on raw data.
layout: 3 vertical panels, left-to-right, shared time-series strip below with highlighted windows
description: Three columns share one time-series strip along the bottom, labeled 'Massive Time Series Database'. The left column, Text-to-SQL, shows an NLQ speech bubble with an arrow to an SQL magnifier icon. A dashed arrow runs down toward the signal and is blocked by a red X marked 'Failure: Morphology Gap'. The right column, Time Series Model, shows a robot icon with a dashed arrow and a red X marked 'Failure: Limited Context'. The wide center column, Sonar-TS, is the visual focus. It runs NLQ to SQL, then SQL Search into stacked 'Multi-scale Feature Tables (Queryable Index)'. Blue beams fan out from the index to three orange candidate windows on the signal. A large magnifying glass labeled 'Verify', a Python logo and a green check show Python verification.
caption: Comparison of querying paradigms. While Text-to-SQL fails to express morphological intents and Time Series Models are limited by context length, Sonar-TS adopts a "Search-Then-Verify" pipeline: it uses SQL to search a symbolic index for candidates and Python to verify them on raw data.
abstract: Natural Language Querying for Time Series Databases (NLQ4TSDB) aims to assist non-expert users retrieve meaningful events, intervals, and summaries from massive temporal records. However, existing Text-to-SQL methods are not designed for continuous morphological intents such as shapes or anomalies, while time series models struggle to handle ultra-long histories. To address these challenges, we propose Sonar-TS, a neuro-symbolic framework that tackles NLQ4TSDB via a Search-Then-Verify pipeline. Analogous to active sonar, it utilizes a feature index to ping candidate windows via SQL, followed by generated Python programs to lock on and verify candidates against raw signals. To enable effective evaluation, we introduce NLQTSBench, the first large-scale benchmark designed for NLQ over TSDB-scale histories. Our experiments highlight the unique challenges within this domain and demonstrate that Sonar-TS effectively navigates complex temporal queries where traditional methods fail. This work presents the first systematic study of NLQ4TSDB, offering a general framework and evaluation standard to facilitate future research.
